GraphNodeService（C#）

Service introduction

GraphNodeService is responsible for node operations within * the subgraph node (GraphNode). In the Atom platform, a main graph can contain subgraph nodes (GraphNode), and the subgraph also has its own node topology inside. The interface design of GraphNodeService is highly symmetrical to NodeService. The difference is that each method requires an additional input of graphNodeId (ID of the subgraph node) to locate the subgraph level where the operation target is located. All methods are asynchronous.

namespace: AtomSdk.Services

Entrance: client.GraphNode

Applicable scenarios

  • Operate nodes inside a subgraph node (GraphNode) in the main graph;

  • Create, delete, and connect nodes within the subgraph to form the calculation logic within the subgraph;

  • Read and write parameters and port data of nodes in the subgraph;

  • Activate, initialize, update, or run nodes inside subgraph nodes;

  • Run the entire subgraph directly (RunGraphAsync).

Relation to NodeService

Compare dimensions NodeService GraphNodeService

Operation object

Nodes in the main graph Nodes inside the

subgraph node (GraphNode)

Extra parameters

None

requires graphNodeId (subgraph node ID)

Interface signature

NodeRef, PortRef and other parameter objects

SubGraphNodeRef, SubGraphPortRef and other parameter objects

Special interface

None

RunGraphAsync (run the entire subgraph)

Recommended calling order

client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync(graphName)    (Open the main image first)
        ↓
OpenGraphAsync(SubGraphRef)              (Open subplot,Refresh timestamp)
        ↓
CreateNodeAsync(SubGraphCreateNodeParams)          (Create nodes in subgraph)
        ↓
SetNodeParamDataAsync(SubGraphNodeParamUpdate)     (Set node parameters in subgraph)
        |
        ↓
ConnectNodesAsync(SubGraphConnectionParams)        (Connect node ports in subgraph)
        ↓
RunGraphAsync(SubGraphRef)               (Run the entire subgraph,Polling waiting for completion)

Interface detailed explanation

OpenGraphAsync(…​)

// original JsonElement version
Task<JsonElement> OpenGraphAsync(
    SubGraphRef paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Generic version
Task<T> OpenGraphAsync<T>(
    SubGraphRef paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

// Strongly typed convenience version
Task<GraphOpenResult> OpenGraphInfoAsync(
    SubGraphRef paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Purpose: Open the specified subgraph node, refresh and obtain the current timestamp of the subgraph (this method must be called before any editing of the internal nodes of the subgraph).

Parameters

Name type Description

graphName

string

Main image name

graphNodeId

string

ID of the subgraph node (GraphNode) in the main graph

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, optional

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, including timestamp and other sub-picture information, SDK automatically saves the timestamp.

example

using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Models;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

// Open the main image first
await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync("main_graph");

// Open the subgraph node again
var openResult = await client.GraphNode.OpenGraphInfoAsync(
    new SubGraphRef("main_graph", "subgraph-node-id"));
Console.WriteLine($"Subpicture is open,Timestamp: {openResult.Timestamp}");

Purpose: Activate and run the specified node in the subgraph, SDK polls internally until execution is completed and returns. The default is to wait up to 30 seconds; if it exceeds timeout, throw AtomTimeoutException.

Parameters

Name type Description

graphName

string

Main image name

graphNodeId

string

Subgraph node ID

nodeId

string

Node ID in subgraph

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, used by the caller to actively cancel

timeout

TimeSpan?

SDK polling wait timeout; null uses the default 30 seconds, Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan means waiting forever

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, node running result.

example

using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Models;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

var result = await client.GraphNode.ActivateNodeResultAsync(
    new SubGraphNodeRef("main_graph", "subgraph-node-id", "inner-node-id"),
    timeout: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60));
Console.WriteLine($"Node activation in subgraph completed,Request status: {result.Status}");

RunGraphAsync(…​) (subgraph-specific)

// original JsonElement version(Polling waiting for completion)
Task<JsonElement> RunGraphAsync(
    SubGraphRef paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    TimeSpan? timeout = null)

// Generic version
Task<T> RunGraphAsync<T>(
    SubGraphRef paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    TimeSpan? timeout = null)

// Strongly typed convenience version
Task<NodeRunResult> RunGraphResultAsync(
    SubGraphRef paramsData,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default,
    TimeSpan? timeout = null)

Purpose: Run the entire subgraph node (triggering the execution of all nodes in the subgraph in topological order), SDK polls internally until it is completed and returns. The default is to wait up to 30 seconds; if it exceeds timeout, throw AtomTimeoutException. This is a method unique to GraphNodeService, and there is no corresponding interface in NodeService.

Parameters

Name type Description

graphName

string

Main image name

graphNodeId

string

Subgraph node ID

cancellationToken

CancellationToken

Cancellation token, used by the caller to actively cancel

timeout

TimeSpan?

SDK polling wait timeout; null uses the default 30 seconds, Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan means waiting forever

Return value: Task<JsonElement>, the summary result after the subgraph is completed.

example

using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Models;

var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");

await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync("main_graph");

// Run the entire subgraph,most wait 60 seconds
var result = await client.GraphNode.RunGraphResultAsync(
    new SubGraphRef("main_graph", "subgraph-node-id"),
    timeout: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60));
Console.WriteLine($"Subgraph execution completed,Request status: {result.Status}");

Complete example

The following example demonstrates finding a subgraph node in the main graph, opening and configuring the subgraph, and finally running the subgraph:

using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Core;
using AtomSdk.Models;

class GraphNodeWorkflowExample
{
    static async Task Main()
    {
        var client = new AtomClient("http://localhost:8080");
        const string mainGraph = "main_pipeline";
        const string subgraphNodeId = "subgraph-node-001";

        try
        {
            // 1. Open main image
            await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync(mainGraph);
            Console.WriteLine("[1] The main image is open");

            // 2. Open subgraph node(Get subgraph timestamp)
            var subOpen = await client.GraphNode.OpenGraphInfoAsync(
                new SubGraphRef(mainGraph, subgraphNodeId));
            Console.WriteLine($"[2] Subpicture is open,Timestamp: {subOpen.Timestamp}");

            // 3. Create nodes within a subgraph
            var preprocessNode = await client.GraphNode.CreateNodeInfoAsync(
                new SubGraphCreateNodeParams(
                    mainGraph, subgraphNodeId, "PreprocessNode", "Image preprocessing"));
            var modelNode = await client.GraphNode.CreateNodeInfoAsync(
                new SubGraphCreateNodeParams(
                    mainGraph, subgraphNodeId, "InferenceNode", "Model reasoning"));
            Console.WriteLine($"[3] The creation of nodes in the subgraph is completed: {preprocessNode.NodeId}, {modelNode.NodeId}, Request status={modelNode.Status}");

            // 4. Set model node parameters
            await client.GraphNode.SetNodeParamDataAsync(
                new SubGraphNodeParamUpdate(
                    mainGraph, subgraphNodeId, modelNode.NodeId,
                    "model_path", "init_params", "/models/detector.onnx"));
            Console.WriteLine("[4] Parameters have been set");

            // 5. Connect nodes within a subgraph
            await client.GraphNode.ConnectNodesAsync(
                new SubGraphConnectionParams(
                    mainGraph, subgraphNodeId,
                    outputNodeId: preprocessNode.NodeId, outputPortName: "output",
                    inputNodeId: modelNode.NodeId, inputPortName: "input"));
            Console.WriteLine("[5] Nodes in the subgraph are connected");

            // 6. Set the binding name for the output port
            await client.GraphNode.SetBindingNameAsync(
                new SubGraphBindingUpdate(
                    mainGraph, subgraphNodeId, modelNode.NodeId,
                    "outputs", "predictions", "subgraph_output"));
            Console.WriteLine("[6] Binding name is set");

            // 7. Run the entire subgraph,most wait 30 seconds
            var runResult = await client.GraphNode.RunGraphResultAsync(
                new SubGraphRef(mainGraph, subgraphNodeId),
                timeout: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
            Console.WriteLine($"[7] Subgraph execution completed,Request status: {runResult.Status}");

            // 8. Read the output node port data in the subgraph
            var output = await client.GraphNode.GetNodePortDataAsync(
                new SubGraphPortRef(
                    mainGraph, subgraphNodeId, modelNode.NodeId,
                    "predictions", "outputs"));
            Console.WriteLine($"[8] Output data: {output}");
        }
        catch (AtomApiException ex)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Server error {ex.Status}: {ex.Message}");
        }
        catch (AtomHttpException ex)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"HTTP Error {ex.StatusCode}: {ex.Message}");
        }
    }
}
